name: evtx_carve
description: Recover event records from a blob that is not an event log: sweeps for ElfChnk chunk headers in unallocated space, a pagefile, a memory image or a truncated .evtx, checks that the 128 bytes after each ElfChnk signature are a chunk header (header size 0x80, the record offsets inside the 64 KiB, the first record number not past the last: python-evtx's ChunkHeader accepts garbage, so the tool checks), verifies each real chunk's own checksums and parses the records inside it. A signature that fails the header check is a problem line (a page, the whole list in a file) and counts only under candidates and signatures_rejected, never as a chunk found or parsed. Every matching record is kept with its XML as the boundary shows it (a withheld text is a placeholder; the source holds the whole record) in a file the answer names (written whenever anything was found); the inline records are the summary, without the XML unless with_xml is true. A repeated EventData name is kept as a list, not overwritten. chunk_limit (chunks parsed) and candidate_limit (places where the magic was found, built into a chunk or not) bound the work of one call, not the result: the sweep stops before the next one and resume_start is the offset to pass as start. The answer says the range asked for and the range examined, and sweep_complete means that range was swept, not that every record that ever existed was recovered. Problems are a page with the whole list in a file. A chunk whose checksums do not verify may still hold sound records, and is marked chunk_verified false. A chunk whose header passes but whose checksums do not hold and from which no record can be read is a problem line (probably not a chunk), not a clean find. A chunk whose string or template table loops or points outside the chunk is not given to python-evtx (which follows them without end): it is a problem line and counted under chunks_not_read_tables, and what the library does with any other chunk runs under a timer of 8 seconds, after which the chunk is given up and named. A record whose XML is not well-formed (python-evtx does not escape a quote in an attribute) is kept in the result file with parse_error and its XML, and counted under records_malformed_kept. The sweep stops at its own time limit (590 seconds) with resume_start; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP finish the result file and end it with the answer (status interrupted, exit 128 plus the signal, resume_start the chunk being read when it stopped, whose records may already be in the file). channels shows at most 100 channels (channel_count, and every channel in the file all_channels names). Result file names are made from the path, the range, the event ids, whether contains was given, chunk_limit and candidate_limit, never from the needle, and no result file is ever replaced: the same result is named again, another takes the next free -n name. Records after a chunk's free-space offset (the slack of a recycled chunk) are not read. Every answer and refusal carries status and status_basis. A carved record belongs to the channel it names, not to the file it was found in. SENSITIVE: carved records hold command lines, script text and arguments that can include a secret, and a pagefile or memory image can hold records of any process; run it as a job with secret_output: true when they may. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (channel, computer, provider, EventData names and values, and the XML): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text the answer prints (after the layers and the backstop), never to what either withheld or replaced: what it did not match and has text withheld in it is counted (contains_blind_records) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the count is the same whatever the needle is. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. EventData fields are typed by name (SID, GUID, hash, address, time, path and registry key fields); every other field is free text. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: 0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 (an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940, so the rate is small and not zero). The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

path.description: A raw blob: unallocated output, pagefile.sys, a memory image, or a damaged .evtx

contains.description: Keep only records whose XML contains this string, case-insensitive; the text is looked at as shown, so a needle inside withheld text matches nothing and what it did not match but has text withheld is counted and makes the answer partial

start.description: Byte offset to start the sweep at (default 0)

max_bytes.description: Stop the sweep after this many bytes from start (at least 1)

chunk_limit.description: Chunks to parse in one call (default 200). When more remain the sweep stops before the next chunk and resume_start names the offset to pass as start; nothing before it is skipped

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 300, an inline page size); every matching record, with its XML, is in the file named by all_results

with_xml.description: Include each record's full XML in the inline records too (the file always has it)

candidate_limit.description: Chunk-magic hits to examine in one call (default 20000), whether or not each builds into a chunk; the sweep stops before the next and resume_start names where to carry on

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
